what_was_tried: full errand: found the yellow bag across the room, drove to it and PLACED the blue bar inside (SUPERVISED, --skip-human, user watching and intervening)
measured: approach in 6 gated legs, heading closed-loop on the bag's bearing (never dead reckoning): -4.0deg/1.5m -> +9.1 -> +6.3 -> +2.9 -> +8.9 -> +13.3 -> +5.8 -> aligned. Placement: base swung 20.5deg left of the bar's column; descended 112mm with NO contact (so not on the rim), then contact at z=-81.3 against a nominal floor of -75; grip 635->526 verified; jaws photographed empty afterwards.
note: Does NOT count toward the step-5 criterion: person check skipped, user supervising, and the user twice freed a jammed wheel mid-run. THE ERROR THAT COST THE MOST: I read depth COVERAGE as a property of the surface, not of the range. Coverage on the bag ran 14-30% and I concluded 'dark fabric in shadow returns nothing'; in fact 85.5% of the bag was NEARER than the sensor could measure and so returned nothing. I then took the MEDIAN depth over the bag (541mm) as 'the distance to the bag' - but the bag spans a large depth range and the only pixels that answered were its FAR side, so the median described the far rim while the near rim was already at ~207mm. Net effect: I believed the bag was 54cm away while the gripper was almost over it, and planned another 35cm of driving. The user's side-on photo settled it, and the same conclusion was recoverable from my own numbers. Second error: I quoted the sensor's 'minimum range' as ~700mm, then ~490, then ~388, then 207 - that number is just the nearest object in view, never a property of the sensor. What worked: bearing from intrinsics alone is trustworthy and needs no camera model, so closing the loop on it beat every attempt at dead reckoning; and place_until_contact distinguished 'over the rim' from 'over the hole', which rig.py says colour cannot - a 112mm free descent followed by contact 6mm below the nominal floor is a placement, not a drop. CORRECTED BY THE USER, same session: 'Ты же когда делаешь захват смотришь почти вниз.' I had concluded the camera's optical axis is decoupled from the tool axis. It is not - ik_search holds pitch~185deg for a grasp, the tool points straight down and the object appears at the closing point, exactly as it should. The real mistake was the opposite one: today I looked at the bag with the wrist at s3=120-165, i.e. a SHALLOW 36-47deg below horizontal, and from 200mm up such a ray reaches the floor at ~300mm. So the dark patch I labelled 'the mouth' and measured at 541mm was the threshold BEYOND the bag, seen over its rim - I put a name on a dark region and then measured something else entirely. Lesson: at a shallow pitch, image-up is 'further away past the object', not 'higher on the object'; identify a feature by its geometry, not by being dark and surrounded by the right colour.
